rationale: C09 supplies a concrete termination-proclamation template: identify the earlier proclamation and its underlying transaction, recite statutory authority to terminate it, establish the factual basis and effective date, and proclaim that the earlier proclamation shall terminate. The child's subject is copyright rather than trade, but its operative sequence and key termination language closely track C09. C12 is another strong termination model, while C04 shares the child's copyright-extension terminology but performs the opposite action and lacks the termination structure.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Whereas the said section 9 of title 17 of the United States Code authorizes the President to terminate any such proclamation at any time
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Whereas the said section 350(a) of the Tariff Act of 1930 authorizes the President to terminate in whole or in part any proclamation carrying out a trade agreement entered into under such section
shared_material.explanation: Both expressly recite statutory authority to terminate an earlier proclamation immediately before the operative clause.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Whereas it appears that ... termination of the proclamation as of that date would be in the interest of the United States of America
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Whereas the Government of the United States of America has agreed ... that the said trade agreement shall cease to be in force on and after December 1, 1949
shared_material.explanation: Both establish a factual predicate for ending the prior regime on a specified date.

shared_material.child_excerpt: do hereby proclaim that the aforesaid [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE] of March 10, 1944, and the extension of time granted thereby, shall terminate on December 29, 1950
shared_material.parent_excerpt: do hereby proclaim that the said proclamation dated April 20, 1936, shall terminate and cease to have effect at the close of November 30, 1949
shared_material.explanation: The operative provisions share the distinctive formulation proclaiming that an identified earlier proclamation shall terminate on a specified date.
